title: RGENGY — RotoGrinders Data Quality Audit
description: Open, auditable rebuild of the data quality behind RotoGrinders' DFS projection system: what it uses, where that data comes from, what could be verified from official sources and — equally — what could not. At commit d758f87 the README's own generated statistics block reads audit date 2026-09-22, 460 tests passing, 16 registered endpoints, 11 scoring tables and 34 findings on the register, and each of those was independently re-counted in this audit: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests` ran 460 tests OK, rgengy/data/scoring/ holds 11 JSON tables (MLB across DraftKings, FanDuel and Yahoo, NBA, NFL, NHL and WNBA across DraftKings and FanDuel), rgengy/findings.py carries 28 IR-nn irregularities plus 6 L-nn limitations, and `python3 -m rgengy sources` prints 16 endpoints, 14 official, 2 unofficial, 0 requiring auth. The headline result is an external validation: RGENGY's independently sourced DraftKings MLB coefficients, applied to RotoGrinders' own published stat projections, reproduce the published FPTS for all 6 free rows within 0.07 FPTS (0.56 percent worst case), and FPTS per dollar reproduces exactly as FPTS / (SALARY / 1000) with a maximum error of 0.0036 over those 6 rows — the only RotoGrinders analytic column the project claims to reproduce. Counting the tables value by value, 122 coefficients across 9 of the 11 carry confirmed_by_operator true. Anything that could not be verified is null with a written reason: RotoGrinders' OBFPTS, TOPVAL, DIFFERENCE, OPTO and TEAMOWN columns have no published formula.

flags: Two of the README's own counts disagree with the repository at the same commit. Its headline table says '15 live-verified … 1 reachable-only' while `python3 -m rgengy sources` prints documented=1, live-verified=14, reachable=1; and L-02 says the operator retrievals confirmed '122 coefficients across 7 of the 11 tables' while the 122 per-value confirmed_by_operator flags are spread across 9 tables. The counted values are published here. IRR-79.

The audit moved while it was being read. This entry was first counted at commit 8300513, where the same commands returned 459 tests, 29 findings and endpoint status documented=3, live-verified=9, reachable=1, unverified=3; pass 3 then landed as babac1f and d758f87 ('repair what the first live CI verify run exposed; publish it'), taking the suite to 460 and the register to 34. Every figure below is re-taken at the later head.

L-02 is the binding constraint and it is stated rather than hidden: the build sandbox has no raw-socket network access so the live pipeline is exercised by CI rather than locally, DraftKings' canonical in-app rules page (the document of record) remains unretrieved, and MLB caught stealing (IR-04) and the DraftKings quality-start question (IR-05) stay flagged. Five defects found in RGENGY itself are on the register, two of them surfaced by the project's own live CI verify run — a mis-encoded ESPN URL and a checker that scored healthy HTML pages as failures — each fixed and pinned by tests.

IR-18 was reversed twice, and the second reversal undid the audit's own correction: pass 2 set the NFL 100- and 300-yard bonuses to 0.0 on the strength of two 2026 secondary sources, then FanDuel's own rules page showed that both operators do pay them, so the secondary sources were wrong and the 'correction' was the error.

The Pages workflow uploads site/ as an Actions artifact (actions/upload-pages-artifact with path: site, then actions/deploy-pages), but GET /repos/buffedlizard55-lab/RGENGY/pages reports build_type legacy with source main / and there is no index.html at the root, so the published URL is a Jekyll render of the branch root rather than the built site in site/. Classified stub on that basis. IRR-76.
